summary: The scatter plot compares crude excess death rates to age-standardized excess death rates per 100,000 population across WHO regions for 2020–2021. Most data points lie below the diagonal line, indicating that crude excess death rates tend to be higher than age-standardized rates in many regions. The European Region shows the highest crude excess death rates, while the Region of the Americas shows relatively high age-standardized excess death rates. The Western Pacific Region has the lowest excess death rates overall.
